<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Implement Billing slice">
Implement the Billing slice (story 836) in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm: CleanerCrm.Billing context (Invoice, Payment schemas + StripeGateway module + migration), CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive (Index + Show), CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController (public /pay/:token), and a Stripe webhook endpoint (POST /webhooks/stripe).

FIRST: call mcp start_task with requirement_name="implementation_file", entity_type="component", module_name="CleanerCrm.Billing", then per child/surface (Invoice, Payment, StripeGateway, CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Index, CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show, CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController). If module_name isn't accepted, resolve via list_requirements module_filter="Billing"/"Invoice"/"Payment".

Acceptance contract: test/spex/836_invoice_completed_jobs_and_collect_payment/ — read ALL 6 files. Job completion → invoice generated (subscribe to a completion event or expose Billing.generate_for_job called by the completion flow — since FieldLive.Job doesn't exist yet, expose the function AND wire a hook in Scheduling job status transition ONLY if scheduling.ex has a clean seam; otherwise leave a documented integration point); auto-charge card on file (state changes ONLY on webhook confirmation per ADR payments-stripe — the "charged" step means PaymentIntent created + receipt, "paid" only on webhook); no card → payment link at public /pay/:token (ConnTest-driven); declined via webhook; invoice shows proof-of-work from CleanerCrm.Quality (being built concurrently — reference by function name per the fixtures contract CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(scope, %{job_id:, amount:, status:}) and read Quality data defensively). Stripe calls behind StripeGateway behaviour with a Test adapter — no live Stripe in tests; verify webhook signatures in the real adapter. Money: integer cents.

Depends on Scheduling (stable, read-only) and Clients (read-only; client card_on_file flag exists in fixtures contract). Do NOT modify scheduling*, schedule_live/*, client_live/*, quoting*, notifications*, quality*, time_tracking* (other agents own them). Router: InvoiceLive routes in authenticated live_session; /pay/:token + /webhooks/stripe public.

Verify: mix compile clean, mix format, MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate, `mix spex test/spex/836_invoice_completed_jobs_and_collect_payment/` (7153 drives FieldLive completion → stays red; others should pass; report counts), `mix test` no regressions.

Final response: files, 836 pass counts, blockers. Under 150 words.
</teammate-message>

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7153Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7153 — Completing a job generates its invoice
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "marking a job complete generates its invoice" do
    scenario "completing a job generates its invoice" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a scheduled job has an agreed price of $150", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :scheduled
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner marks the job complete", context do
        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        job_live
        |> element("[data-test='mark-complete-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :job_live, job_live)}
      end

      then_ "the job is shown as complete to the cleaner", context do
        assert render(context.job_live) =~ "Complete"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "an invoice for $150 appears in the owner's billing queue", context do
        {:ok, _invoices_live, html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices")

        assert html =~ context.client.name
        assert html =~ "$150.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.
4	
5	  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
6	  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
7	  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.
8	
9	  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
10	  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
11	  """
12	
13	  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]
14	
15	  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
16	  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
17	  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
18	  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
19	            [
20	              CleanerCrm.Clients,
21	              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
22	              CleanerCrm.Quality,
23	              CleanerCrm.Billing,
24	              CleanerCrm.TimeTracking,
25	              CleanerCrm.Notifications
26	            ]}
27	
28	  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
29	  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
30	  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
31	  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
32	  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
33	  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
34	  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
35	  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
36	
37	  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
38	  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
39	  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
40	  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
41	    {:ok, account} =
42	      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
43	        scope,
44	        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
45	      )

51	  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
52	  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
53	
54	  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
55	  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
56	  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
57	  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
58	  # cleaner assignment directly.

60	    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
61	    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
62	    user
63	  end

66	  #
67	  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
68	  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
69	  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
70	  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,

72	  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
73	  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures do
  @moduledoc """
  Curated bridge from BDD specs into in-app state.

  The only module that may dep on `CleanerCrm` from inside the spex test
  tree. Declared as its own top-level Boundary so the spec boundary
  (`CleanerCrmSpex`) can dep on it without inheriting `CleanerCrm`'s deps.

  Keep this list small — every export is a sanctioned shortcut past the
  UI, used only for `given_` state that has its own covered creation flow.
  """

  use Boundary, top_level?: true, deps: [CleanerCrm, CleanerCrmTest]

  # These contexts are specified in the architecture but not yet
  # implemented — the red BDD specs that call these fixtures exist to
  # drive their implementation. Remove entries as each context lands.
  @compile {:no_warn_undefined,
            [
              CleanerCrm.Clients,
              CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
              CleanerCrm.Quality,
              CleanerCrm.Billing,
              CleanerCrm.TimeTracking,
              CleanerCrm.Notifications
            ]}

  # Auth/session seeding — registration and login have their own specs;
  # every other spec starts from an existing confirmed user.
  defdelegate user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate unconfirmed_user_fixture(attrs \\ %{}), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate user_scope_fixture(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate valid_user_password(), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  defdelegate set_password(user), to: CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures

  # Tenant seeding — account creation has its own spec; other specs need
  # an existing company (account) to scope against.
  # Uncertain export: prune if account specs end up seeding via the UI.
  def account_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, account} =
      CleanerCrm.Accounts.create_account(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{name: "Sparkle Co #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"})
      )

    account
  end

  # Session — logs a fixture user into a conn. Login itself has its
  # own auth specs; every other spec starts from an authenticated conn.
  defdelegate log_in_user(conn, user), to: CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  # Scheduling (story 834) — a cleaner is an account member who gets
  # assigned jobs. No creation flow covers this yet: `ScheduleLive.Board`
  # (the board's own assign/reassign UI) doesn't exist. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — prune once the board can seed
  # cleaner assignment directly.
  def cleaner_fixture(scope, account, attrs \\ %{}) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture(attrs)
    {:ok, _member} = CleanerCrm.Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account.id, :member)
    user
  end

  # Billing (story 836) — client, job, and invoice seeding.
  #
  # Job completion generating its invoice is covered end-to-end by
  # story 836's own "completing a job generates its invoice" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job -> InvoiceLive). Scenarios whose subject is
  # a downstream invoice-collection decision (charging a card,
  # payment links, declines, webhook confirmation) seed the completed
  # job and its invoice directly here instead of re-driving job
  # completion every time — a sanctioned shortcut per
  # bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def client_fixture(scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, client} =
      CleanerCrm.Clients.create_client(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          name: "Client #{System.unique_integer([:positive])}",
          card_on_file: false
        })
      )

    client
  end

  def job_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, job} =
      CleanerCrm.Scheduling.create_job(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          agreed_price: Decimal.new("150.00"),
          status: :scheduled
        })
      )

    job
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scope,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
4	  conflict-aware assignment.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
7	  """
8	
9	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
10	
11	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
12	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
14	
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
16	    AvailabilityBlock,
17	    ConflictDetector,
18	    Job,
19	    Recurrence,
20	    RecurringPlan
21	  }
22	
23	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
24	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User
25	
26	  ## Jobs
27	
28	  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
29	    Job
30	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
31	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
32	    |> Repo.get!(id)
33	  end
34	
35	  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
36	    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
37	  end
38	
39	  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
40	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
41	    with {:ok, job} <-
42	           %Job{account_id: account_id}
43	           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
44	           |> Repo.insert() do
45	      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
46	        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
47	        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
48	      })
49	
50	      {:ok, job}
51	    end
52	  end
53	
54	  @doc """
55	  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
56	  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
57	  """
58	  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
59	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
60	    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)
61	
62	    Job
63	    |> where(
64	      [j],
65	      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
66	        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
67	    )
68	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
69	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
70	    |> Repo.all()
71	  end
72	
73	  @doc """
74	  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
75	  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
76	  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
77	  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
78	  """
79	  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
80	    Job
81	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
82	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
83	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
84	    |> Repo.all()
85	  end
86	
87	  @doc """
88	  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
89	  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
90	  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
91	  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
92	  """
93	  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
94	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
95	    with :ok <-
96	           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
97	             scope,
98	             cleaner_id,
99	             job.scheduled_date,
100	             job.start_time,
101	             job.end_time,
102	             exclude_job_id: job.id
103	           ),
104	         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
105	      Recorder.record(
106	        scope,
107	        "job_reassigned",
108	        "Job",
109	        updated.id,
110	        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
111	        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
112	      )
113	
114	      {:ok, updated}
115	    end
116	  end
117	
118	  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
119	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
120	    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
121	      Recorder.record(
122	        scope,
123	        "job_cancelled",
124	        "Job",
125	        updated.id,
126	        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
127	        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
128	      )
129	
130	      {:ok, updated}
131	    end
132	  end
133	
134	  ## Recurring plans
135	
136	  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
137	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
138	    RecurringPlan
139	    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
140	    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
141	    |> Repo.get!(id)
142	  end
143	
144	  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
145	    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
146	  end
147	
148	  @doc """
149	  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
150	  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
151	  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
152	  """
153	  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
154	    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
155	  end
156	
157	  @doc """
158	  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
159	  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
160	  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
161	  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
162	  """
163	  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
164	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
165	    Repo.transact(fn ->
166	      with {:ok, plan} <-
167	             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
168	             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
169	             |> Repo.insert() do
170	        jobs =
171	          plan
172	          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
173	          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
174	            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
175	            job
176	          end)
177	
178	        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
179	      end
180	    end)
181	  end
182	
183	  ## Availability blocks
184	
185	  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
186	    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(attrs)
           |> Repo.insert() do
      Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, %{
        "scheduled_date" => to_string(job.scheduled_date),
        "cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id
      })

      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id and j.status != :cancelled)
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while every other caller (fixtures, other
  # contexts) uses the schema's real field name directly.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

2	  @moduledoc """

102	    |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
103	    |> Repo.insert()

112	        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
113	        %Property{} = property,
114	        attrs
115	      )
116	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
117	    changeset =

120	      |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
121

123	      record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, updated.id)

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients do
  @moduledoc """
  Clients and their properties: addresses, parking notes, entry
  methods and codes, pets, and cleaning preferences — the authoritative
  access and scope record every job carries.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.{Client, Property}
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder

  ## Clients

  def list_clients(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([c], asc: c.name)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_client!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Client
    |> where([c], c.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Client{account_id: account_id}
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  def change_client(%Scope{}, %Client{} = client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Client.changeset(client, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Lists only active clients, for the account's day-to-day client list.
  """
  def list_active_clients(%Scope{} = scope) do
    scope |> list_clients() |> Enum.filter(& &1.active)
  end

  def update_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    client
    |> Client.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  def deactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => false})
  end

  def reactivate_client(%Scope{} = scope, %Client{} = client) do
    update_client(scope, client, %{"active" => true})
  end

  @doc """
  Permanently deletes a client and its properties.

  Refuses to delete a client that still has dependent records (e.g.
  scheduled jobs) elsewhere in the system — the database's foreign key
  constraints are the source of truth for what's "dependent," so this
  context stays ignorant of any other bounded context's schema.
  """
  def delete_client(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{} = client)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.delete(client)
  rescue
    Ecto.ConstraintError -> {:error, :has_upcoming_jobs}
  end

  ## Properties

  @doc """
  Lists a client's properties, ordered by address.
  """
  def list_properties(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Client{id: client_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id and p.client_id == ^client_id)
    |> order_by([p], asc: p.service_address)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  def get_property!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Property
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def create_property(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Property{account_id: account_id}
    |> Property.changeset(attrs)
    |> validate_client_ownership(scope)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a property. When entry method, lockbox code, or alarm code
  change, records an audit entry naming the changed fields (never the
  code values themselves).
  """
  def update_property(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope,
        %Property{} = property,
        attrs
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset =
      property
      |> Property.changeset(attrs)
      |> validate_client_ownership(scope)

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, updated.id)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def change_property(%Scope{}, %Property{} = property, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Property.changeset(property, attrs)
  end

  defp validate_client_ownership(changeset, %Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) do
    case Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, :client_id) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      client_id ->
        query = where(Client, [c], c.id == ^client_id and c.account_id == ^account_id)

        if Repo.exists?(query) do
          changeset
        else
          Ecto.Changeset.add_error(changeset, :client_id, "is invalid")
        end
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists audit entries recorded against a property, most recent first.
  """
  def list_property_audit_entries(%Scope{} = scope, %Property{} = property) do
    Recorder.list_for_subject(scope, "Property", property.id)
  end

  defp record_access_code_changes(scope, changeset, property_id) do
    changed_fields =
      Property.access_code_fields()
      |> Enum.filter(&Ecto.Changeset.get_change(changeset, &1))
      |> Enum.map(&to_string/1)

    case changed_fields do
      [] ->
        :ok

      fields ->
        Recorder.record(scope, "access_details_updated", "Property", property_id, %{}, %{
          "changed_fields" => fields
        })
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Client do
  @moduledoc """
  A paying customer with contact info and preferences.

  Scoped to an account: every client belongs to exactly one account and
  is only ever visible within that account.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t() | nil,
          active: boolean(),
          card_on_file: boolean(),
          properties: [CleanerCrm.Clients.Property.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "clients" do
    field :name, :string
    field :active, :boolean, default: true
    field :card_on_file, :boolean, default: false

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    has_many :properties, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(client, attrs) do
    client
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :active, :card_on_file])
    |> validate_required([:name], message: "is required")
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 200)
  end
end

  use Mix.Project

  def project do
    [
      app: :cleaner_crm,
      version: "0.1.0",
      elixir: "~> 1.19",
      elixirc_paths: elixirc_paths(Mix.env()),
      start_permanent: Mix.env() == :prod,
      aliases: aliases(),
      deps: deps(),
      compilers: compilers(Mix.env()),
      listeners: [Phoenix.CodeReloader]
    ]
  end

  # Configuration for the OTP application.
  #
  # Type `mix help compile.app` for more information.
  def application do
    [
      mod: {CleanerCrmWeb.Application, []},
      extra_applications: [:logger, :runtime_tools]
    ]
  end

  def cli do
    [
      preferred_envs: [precommit: :test, spex: :test]
    ]
  end

  defp compilers(:test),
    do: [:diagnostics, :boundary, :phoenix_live_view, :erlang, :elixir, :spex, :app]

  defp compilers(_),
    do: [:diagnostics, :boundary, :phoenix_live_view, :erlang, :elixir, :app]

  # Specifies which paths to compile per environment.
  defp elixirc_paths(:test), do: ["lib", "test/support"]
  defp elixirc_paths(_), do: ["lib"]

  # Specifies your project dependencies.
  #
  # Type `mix help deps` for examples and options.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared givens for Cleaner CRM BDD specs.

  Consumer spex modules pull these in with a plain Elixir `import`:

      import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

      scenario "..." do
        given_ :logged_in_owner_with_account
      end

  | Name | Produces | Requires |
  |---|---|---|
  | `:logged_in_owner_with_account` | `context.conn` (authenticated), `context.user`, `context.scope`, `context.account` | `context.conn` |
  """

  use SexySpex.Givens

  import Phoenix.ConnTest
  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

  register_given :logged_in_owner_with_account, context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture() |> Fixtures.set_password()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, login_live, _html} = live(context.conn, "/users/log-in")

    form =
      form(login_live, "#login_form_password",
        user: %{
          email: user.email,
          password: Fixtures.valid_user_password(),
          remember_me: true
        }
      )

    conn = submit_form(form, context.conn)

    {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb do
  @moduledoc """
  The entrypoint for defining your web interface, such
  as controllers, components, channels, and so on.

  This can be used in your application as:

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller
      use CleanerCrmWeb, :html

  The definitions below will be executed for every controller,
  component, etc, so keep them short and clean, focused
  on imports, uses and aliases.

  Do NOT define functions inside the quoted expressions
  below. Instead, define additional modules and import
  those modules here.
  """

  use Boundary, deps: [CleanerCrm], exports: :all

  def static_paths, do: ~w(assets fonts images favicon.ico robots.txt)

  def router do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Router, helpers: false

      # Import common connection and controller functions to use in pipelines
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.Controller
      import Phoenix.LiveView.Router
    end
  end

  def channel do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Channel
    end
  end

  def controller do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Controller, formats: [:html, :json]

      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      import Plug.Conn

      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def live_view do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveView

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def live_component do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveComponent

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def html do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Component

      # Import convenience functions from controllers
      import Phoenix.Controller,
        only: [get_csrf_token: 0, view_module: 1, view_template: 1]

      # Include general helpers for rendering HTML
      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  defp html_helpers do
    quote do
      # Translation
      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      # HTML escaping functionality
      import Phoenix.HTML
      # Core UI components
      import CleanerCrmWeb.CoreComponents

      # Common modules used in templates
      alias Phoenix.LiveView.JS
      alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

      # Routes generation with the ~p sigil
      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def verified_routes do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.VerifiedRoutes,
        endpoint: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
        router: CleanerCrmWeb.Router,
        statics: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths()
    end
  end

  @doc """
  When used, dispatch to the appropriate controller/live_view/etc.
  """
  defmacro __using__(which) when is_atom(which) do
    apply(__MODULE__, which, [])
  end
end

      add :account_id, references(:accounts, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :client_id, references(:clients, type: :binary_id)
      add :property_id, references(:properties, type: :binary_id)
      add :cleaner_id, references(:users, on_delete: :nilify_all)

      add :recurring_plan_id,
          references(:recurring_plans, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :nilify_all)

      add :scheduled_date, :date, null: false
      add :start_time, :time, null: false
      add :end_time, :time, null: false
      add :status, :string, null: false, default: "scheduled"
      add :agreed_price_cents, :integer

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
    end

    create index(:jobs, [:account_id])
    create index(:jobs, [:client_id])
    create index(:jobs, [:property_id])
    create index(:jobs, [:cleaner_id])
    create index(:jobs, [:recurring_plan_id])
    create index(:jobs, [:cleaner_id, :scheduled_date])

    create table(:availability_blocks, primary_key: false) do
      add :id, :binary_id, primary_key: true

      add :account_id, references(:accounts, type: :binary_id, on_delete: :delete_all),
        null: false

      add :cleaner_id, references(:users, on_delete: :delete_all), null: false
      add :date, :date, null: false
      add :all_day, :boolean, null: false, default: false
      add :start_time, :time
      add :end_time, :time

      timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
    end

    create index(:availability_blocks, [:account_id])
    create index(:availability_blocks, [:cleaner_id, :date])

# Payment Processing — Stripe via stripity_stripe

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Story 836 requires invoicing completed jobs and collecting payment via card-on-file or payment link. Research shows payment friction (failed charges, chargebacks) is an acute owner pain; chargeback defense needs proof-of-work attached to invoices.

## Options Considered

- **Stripe (stripity_stripe)** — dominant API, SetupIntents for card-on-file, Payment Links, webhooks; well-maintained Elixir client.
- **Square** — popular with cleaning businesses (Maidily supports it) but weaker Elixir ecosystem.
- **Braintree/PayPal** — no compelling advantage; weaker Elixir support.

## Decision

Use Stripe through the `stripity_stripe` hex package. Card-on-file via Customer + SetupIntent + off-session PaymentIntents; payment links via Stripe Checkout Sessions; webhook endpoint (`CleanerCrmWeb`) confirms payment state transitions. All payment state changes recorded on `CleanerCrm.Billing.Payment` and driven by webhooks, never assumed from API call success.

## Consequences

- Requires Stripe API keys in runtime config (Dotenvy) and a webhook signing secret.
- Test strategy: ReqCassette/fixtures for API calls; webhook handling tested with signed test payloads.
- Square support (relevant to some cleaning businesses) deferred; gateway hidden behind `CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway` so a second gateway can be added later.

1	# Money Handling — integer cents, no money library
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Quotes (835), invoices/payments (836), and pay/earnings (838, 844) all handle money. Research shows pay-transparency disputes are a core cleaner pain, so amounts must never drift from float arithmetic. The product is US-only, USD-only at MVP.
8	
9	## Options Considered
10	
11	- **Integer cents in Postgres** — exact, simple, matches Stripe's amount convention.
12	- **ex_money** — multi-currency correctness we don't need; adds a dependency and custom Ecto types.
13	- **Decimal columns** — exact but invites fractional-cent ambiguity in piece-rate math.
14	
15	## Decision
16	
17	Store all monetary amounts as integer cents (`:integer` columns, `_cents` suffix). Rate math (per-sqft, hourly proration) computes in `Decimal` and rounds half-up to cents at each persisted boundary. A small `CleanerCrm.Money` formatting helper renders `$X.XX`; Stripe amounts pass through unchanged.
18	
19	## Consequences
20	
21	- Multi-currency would require a migration to ex_money later; acceptable for a US-market MVP.
22	- Rounding policy (half-up at persistence boundaries) must be stated in Quoting and TimeTracking specs so earnings and invoice totals always reconcile.
23

file.content:
# Money Handling — integer cents, no money library

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Quotes (835), invoices/payments (836), and pay/earnings (838, 844) all handle money. Research shows pay-transparency disputes are a core cleaner pain, so amounts must never drift from float arithmetic. The product is US-only, USD-only at MVP.

## Options Considered

- **Integer cents in Postgres** — exact, simple, matches Stripe's amount convention.
- **ex_money** — multi-currency correctness we don't need; adds a dependency and custom Ecto types.
- **Decimal columns** — exact but invites fractional-cent ambiguity in piece-rate math.

## Decision

Store all monetary amounts as integer cents (`:integer` columns, `_cents` suffix). Rate math (per-sqft, hourly proration) computes in `Decimal` and rounds half-up to cents at each persisted boundary. A small `CleanerCrm.Money` formatting helper renders `$X.XX`; Stripe amounts pass through unchanged.

## Consequences

- Multi-currency would require a migration to ex_money later; acceptable for a US-market MVP.
- Rounding policy (half-up at persistence boundaries) must be stated in Quoting and TimeTracking specs so earnings and invoice totals always reconcile.

defmodule CleanerCrm.Check.Warning.CleanerCrmSpexDenies do
  use Credo.Check,
    id: "CLEANE0001",
    base_priority: :high,
    category: :warning,
    explanations: [
      check: """
      Project-local WHOLE-module denies for BDD spec files (`_spex.exs`).

      Complements the framework `spex_denied_calls` check (function-level
      denies). Specs drive the app only through public surfaces — LiveView
      routes under `CleanerCrmWeb` and the curated `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`
      bridge. Reaching into contexts or the Repo from a spec bypasses the
      seal and turns the spec into a unit test wearing a costume.

      Denied whole modules:

      - `File`, `:file` — real-disk reads bypass the in-memory environment.
      - `Port` — talks to external programs; use cassettes.
      - `CleanerCrm.Repo` — direct DB access bypasses the public surface.
      - All internal contexts: `CleanerCrm.Clients`, `CleanerCrm.Scheduling`,
        `CleanerCrm.Quoting`, `CleanerCrm.Billing`, `CleanerCrm.Notifications`,
        `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking`, `CleanerCrm.Quality`, `CleanerCrm.Audit`,
        `CleanerCrm.Users`, `CleanerCrm.Accounts`, `CleanerCrm.Integrations` —
        the spec boundary deps only on `CleanerCrmTest` and `CleanerCrmWeb`.

      Seed state through `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`, act through the UI.
      """
    ]

  @denied_whole_modules [
    File,
    Port,
    CleanerCrm.Repo,
    CleanerCrm.Clients,
    CleanerCrm.Scheduling,
    CleanerCrm.Quoting,
    CleanerCrm.Billing,
    CleanerCrm.Notifications,
    CleanerCrm.TimeTracking,
    CleanerCrm.Quality,
    CleanerCrm.Audit,
    CleanerCrm.Users,
    CleanerCrm.Accounts,
    CleanerCrm.Integrations
  ]

  @denied_whole_erlang_modules [:file]

  @doc false
  @impl true
  def run(%SourceFile{filename: filename} = source_file, params) do
    if String.ends_with?(filename, "_spex.exs") do
      ctx = %{issue_meta: Context.build(source_file, params, __MODULE__), issues: []}
      Credo.Code.prewalk(source_file, &traverse/2, ctx).issues
    else
      []
    end
  end

  # Aliased Elixir modules — File.*, Port.*, CleanerCrm.<Context>.*
  defp traverse(
         {{:., _, [{:__aliases__, meta, module_parts}, fun]}, _, _args} = ast,
         ctx
       ) do
    module = Module.concat(module_parts)

    if module in @denied_whole_modules do
      {ast, add_issue(ctx, meta, "#{inspect(module)}.#{fun}")}
    else
      {ast, ctx}
    end
  end

  # Erlang modules — :file.*
  defp traverse({{:., _, [erl_mod, fun]}, meta, _args} = ast, ctx)
       when is_atom(erl_mod) do
    if erl_mod in @denied_whole_erlang_modules do
      {ast, add_issue(ctx, meta, "#{inspect(erl_mod)}.#{fun}")}
    else
      {ast, ctx}
    end
  end

  defp traverse(ast, ctx), do: {ast, ctx}

  defp add_issue(ctx, meta, trigger) do
    issue =
      format_issue(
        ctx.issue_meta,
        message:
          "Call to `#{trigger}` is denied in _spex.exs files. Seed state through " <>
            "CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures and act through the public CleanerCrmWeb surfaces. " <>
            "See .code_my_spec/knowledge/bdd/spex/boundaries.md.",
        trigger: trigger,
        line_no: meta[:line],
        column: meta[:column]
      )

    %{ctx | issues: [issue | ctx.issues]}
  end
end

import Config

# config/runtime.exs is executed for all environments, including
# during releases. It is executed after compilation and before the
# system starts, so it is typically used to load production configuration
# and secrets from environment variables or elsewhere. Do not define
# any compile-time configuration in here, as it won't be applied.
# The block below contains prod specific runtime configuration.

# ## Using releases
#
# If you use `mix release`, you need to explicitly enable the server
# by passing the PHX_SERVER=true when you start it:
#
#     PHX_SERVER=true bin/cleaner_crm start
#
# Alternatively, you can use `mix phx.gen.release` to generate a `bin/server`
# script that automatically sets the env var above.
if System.get_env("PHX_SERVER") do
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint, server: true
end

config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  http: [port: String.to_integer(System.get_env("PORT", "4100"))]

# CodeMySpec feedback widget / OAuth provider credentials.
# Generate the client ID/secret on the CodeMySpec project page and set them
# as env vars before deploying.
config :cleaner_crm,
  codemyspec_url: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_URL") || "https://codemyspec.com",
  codemyspec_client_id: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_ID"),
  codemyspec_client_secret: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_SECRET")

if config_env() == :prod do
  # Encrypted-token vault key — required in production.
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Vault,
    ciphers: [
      default:
        {Cloak.Ciphers.AES.GCM,
         tag: "AES.GCM.V1",
         key:
           Base.decode64!(
             System.get_env("CLOAK_KEY") ||
               raise("environment variable CLOAK_KEY is missing (base64 32-byte key)")
           )}
    ]
end

if config_env() == :prod do
  database_url =
    System.get_env("DATABASE_URL") ||
      raise """
      environment variable DATABASE_URL is missing.
      For example: ecto://USER:PASS@HOST/DATABASE
      """

  maybe_ipv6 = if System.get_env("ECTO_IPV6") in ~w(true 1), do: [:inet6], else: []

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Repo,
    # ssl: true,
    url: database_url,
    pool_size: String.to_integer(System.get_env("POOL_SIZE") || "10"),
    # For machines with several cores, consider starting multiple pools of `pool_size`
    # pool_count: 4,
    socket_options: maybe_ipv6

  # The secret key base is used to sign/encrypt cookies and other secrets.
  # A default value is used in config/dev.exs and config/test.exs but you
  # want to use a different value for prod and you most likely don't want
  # to check this value into version control, so we use an environment
  # variable instead.
  secret_key_base =
    System.get_env("SECRET_KEY_BASE") ||
      raise """
      environment variable SECRET_KEY_BASE is missing.
      You can generate one by calling: mix phx.gen.secret
      """

  host = System.get_env("PHX_HOST") || "example.com"

  config :cleaner_crm, :dns_cluster_query, System.get_env("DNS_CLUSTER_QUERY")

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
    url: [host: host, port: 443, scheme: "https"],
    http: [
      # Enable IPv6 and bind on all interfaces.
      # Set it to  {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1} for local network only access.
      # See the documentation on https://bandit.hexdocs.pm/Bandit.html#t:options/0
      # for details about using IPv6 vs IPv4 and loopback vs public addresses.
      ip: {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
    ],
    secret_key_base: secret_key_base

  # ## SSL Support
  #
  # To get SSL working, you will need to add the `https` key
  # to your endpoint configuration:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  #       https: [
  #         ...,
  #         port: 443,
  #         cipher_suite: :strong,
  #         keyfile: System.get_env("SOME_APP_SSL_KEY_PATH"),
  #         certfile: System.get_env("SOME_APP_SSL_CERT_PATH")
  #       ]
  #
  # The `cipher_suite` is set to `:strong` to support only the
  # latest and more secure SSL ciphers. This means old browsers
  # and clients may not be supported. You can set it to
  # `:compatible` for wider support.
  #
  # `:keyfile` and `:certfile` expect an absolute path to the key
  # and cert in disk or a relative path inside priv, for example
  # "priv/ssl/server.key". For all supported SSL configuration
  # options, see https://plug.hexdocs.pm/Plug.SSL.html#configure/1
  #
  # We also recommend setting `force_ssl` in your config/prod.exs,
  # ensuring no data is ever sent via http, always redirecting to https:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  #       force_ssl: [hsts: true]
  #
  # Check `Plug.SSL` for all available options in `force_ssl`.

  # ## Configuring the mailer
  #
  # In production you need to configure the mailer to use a different adapter.
  # Here is an example configuration for Mailgun:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Mailer,
  #       adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Mailgun,
  #       api_key: System.get_env("MAILGUN_API_KEY"),
  #       domain: System.get_env("MAILGUN_DOMAIN")
  #
  # Most non-SMTP adapters require an API client. Swoosh supports Req, Hackney,
  # and Finch out-of-the-box. This configuration is typically done at
  # compile-time in your config/prod.exs:
  #
  #     config :swoosh, :api_client, Swoosh.ApiClient.Req
  #
  # See https://swoosh.hexdocs.pm/Swoosh.html#module-installation for details.
end

import Config

# Only in tests, remove the complexity from the password hashing algorithm
config :bcrypt_elixir, :log_rounds, 1

# Configure your database
#
# The MIX_TEST_PARTITION environment variable can be used
# to provide built-in test partitioning in CI environment.
# Run `mix help test` for more information.
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Repo,
  username: "postgres",
  password: "postgres",
  hostname: "localhost",
  database: "cleaner_crm_test#{System.get_env("MIX_TEST_PARTITION")}",
  pool: Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox,
  pool_size: System.schedulers_online() * 2

# We don't run a server during test. If one is required,
# you can enable the server option below.
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  http: [ip: {127, 0, 0, 1}, port: 4002],
  secret_key_base: "pKeS+s2UVTkO2arvvgQLttUR3McIVtITSdLygq0I9T9C5M+7mGuWBFFVOWsO/ZMR",
  server: false

# In test we don't send emails
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Mailer, adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Test

# Disable swoosh api client as it is only required for production adapters
config :swoosh, :api_client, false

# Print only warnings and errors during test
config :logger, level: :warning

# Initialize plugs at runtime for faster test compilation
config :phoenix, :plug_init_mode, :runtime

# Enable helpful, but potentially expensive runtime checks
config :phoenix_live_view,
  enable_expensive_runtime_checks: true

# Sort query params output of verified routes for robust url comparisons
config :phoenix,
  sort_verified_routes_query_params: true

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint do
  use Phoenix.Endpoint, otp_app: :cleaner_crm

  # The session will be stored in the cookie and signed,
  # this means its contents can be read but not tampered with.
  # Set :encryption_salt if you would also like to encrypt it.
  @session_options [
    store: :cookie,
    key: "_cleaner_crm_key",
    signing_salt: "IOeVZsWZ",
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  socket "/live", Phoenix.LiveView.Socket,
    websocket: [connect_info: [session: @session_options]],
    longpoll: [connect_info: [session: @session_options]]

  # Serve at "/" the static files from "priv/static" directory.
  #
  # When code reloading is disabled (e.g., in production),
  # the `gzip` option is enabled to serve compressed
  # static files generated by running `phx.digest`.
  plug Plug.Static,
    at: "/",
    from: :cleaner_crm,
    gzip: not code_reloading?,
    only: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths(),
    raise_on_missing_only: code_reloading?

  # Code reloading can be explicitly enabled under the
  # :code_reloader configuration of your endpoint.
  if code_reloading? do
    socket "/phoenix/live_reload/socket", Phoenix.LiveReloader.Socket
    plug Phoenix.LiveReloader
    plug Phoenix.CodeReloader
    plug Phoenix.Ecto.CheckRepoStatus, otp_app: :cleaner_crm
  end

  plug Phoenix.LiveDashboard.RequestLogger,
    param_key: "request_logger",
    cookie_key: "request_logger"

  plug Plug.RequestId
  plug Plug.Telemetry, event_prefix: [:phoenix, :endpoint]

  plug Plug.Parsers,
    parsers: [:urlencoded, :multipart, :json],
    pass: ["*/*"],
    json_decoder: Phoenix.json_library()

  plug Plug.MethodOverride
  plug Plug.Head
  plug Plug.Session, @session_options
  plug CleanerCrmWeb.Router
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Integrations.Providers.Codemyspec do
  @moduledoc """
  CodeMySpec OAuth provider implementation.

  Connects to the CodeMySpec platform for issue reporting and feedback.

  Configure in your runtime config:

      config :cleaner_crm,
        codemyspec_url: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_URL") || "https://codemyspec.com",
        codemyspec_client_id: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_ID"),
        codemyspec_client_secret: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_SECRET")
  """

  @behaviour CleanerCrm.Integrations.Providers.Behaviour

  @callback_path "/integrations/oauth/callback/codemyspec"

  @impl true
  def config do
    base_url = Application.fetch_env!(:cleaner_crm, :codemyspec_url)
    client_id = Application.fetch_env!(:cleaner_crm, :codemyspec_client_id)
    client_secret = Application.fetch_env!(:cleaner_crm, :codemyspec_client_secret)
    redirect_uri = CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> @callback_path

    [
      client_id: client_id,
      client_secret: client_secret,
      redirect_uri: redirect_uri,
      base_url: base_url,
      authorize_url: "#{base_url}/oauth/authorize",
      token_url: "#{base_url}/oauth/token",
      user_url: "#{base_url}/api/me",
      authorization_params: [
        scope: "read write"
      ]
    ]
  end

  @impl true
  def strategy, do: Assent.Strategy.OAuth2

  @impl true
  def normalize_user(user_data) when is_map(user_data) do
    {:ok,
     %{
       provider_user_id: Map.get(user_data, "id") |> to_string(),
       email: Map.get(user_data, "email"),
       name: Map.get(user_data, "email"),
       username: Map.get(user_data, "email"),
       avatar_url: nil
     }}
  end

  def normalize_user(_user_data), do: {:error, :invalid_user_data}
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Clients.Client do
  @moduledoc """
  A paying customer with contact info and preferences.

  Scoped to an account: every client belongs to exactly one account and
  is only ever visible within that account.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          name: String.t() | nil,
          active: boolean(),
          card_on_file: boolean(),
          properties: [CleanerCrm.Clients.Property.t()] | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "clients" do
    field :name, :string
    field :active, :boolean, default: true
    field :card_on_file, :boolean, default: false

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    has_many :properties, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  def changeset(client, attrs) do
    client
    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :active, :card_on_file])
    |> validate_required([:name], message: "is required")
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 200)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.UserNotifier do
  import Swoosh.Email

  alias CleanerCrm.Mailer
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  # Delivers the email using the application mailer.
  defp deliver(recipient, subject, body) do
    email =
      new()
      |> to(recipient)
      |> from({"CleanerCrm", "contact@example.com"})
      |> subject(subject)
      |> text_body(body)

    with {:ok, _metadata} <- Mailer.deliver(email) do
      {:ok, email}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Deliver instructions to update a user email.
  """
  def deliver_update_email_instructions(user, url) do
    deliver(user.email, "Update email instructions", """

    ==============================

    Hi #{user.email},

    You can change your email by visiting the URL below:

    #{url}

    If you didn't request this change, please ignore this.

    ==============================
    """)
  end

  @doc """
  Deliver instructions to log in with a magic link.
  """
  def deliver_login_instructions(user, url) do
    case user do
      %User{confirmed_at: nil} -> deliver_confirmation_instructions(user, url)
      _ -> deliver_magic_link_instructions(user, url)
    end
  end

  defp deliver_magic_link_instructions(user, url) do
    deliver(user.email, "Log in instructions", """

    ==============================

    Hi #{user.email},

    You can log into your account by visiting the URL below:

    #{url}

    If you didn't request this email, please ignore this.

    ==============================
    """)
  end

  defp deliver_confirmation_instructions(user, url) do
    deliver(user.email, "Confirmation instructions", """

    ==============================

    Hi #{user.email},

    You can confirm your account by visiting the URL below:

    #{url}

    If you didn't create an account with us, please ignore this.

    ==============================
    """)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserSessionController do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  def create(conn, %{"_action" => "confirmed"} = params) do
    create(conn, params, "User confirmed successfully.")
  end

  def create(conn, params) do
    create(conn, params, "Welcome back!")
  end

  # magic link login
  defp create(conn, %{"user" => %{"token" => token} = user_params}, info) do
    case Users.login_user_by_magic_link(token) do
      {:ok, {user, tokens_to_disconnect}} ->
        UserAuth.disconnect_sessions(tokens_to_disconnect)

        conn
        |> put_flash(:info, info)
        |> UserAuth.log_in_user(user, user_params)

      _ ->
        conn
        |> put_flash(:error, "The link is invalid or it has expired.")
        |> redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
    end
  end

  # email + password login
  defp create(conn, %{"user" => user_params}, info) do
    %{"email" => email, "password" => password} = user_params

    if user = Users.get_user_by_email_and_password(email, password) do
      conn
      |> put_flash(:info, info)
      |> UserAuth.log_in_user(user, user_params)
    else
      # In order to prevent user enumeration attacks, don't disclose whether the email is registered.
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "Invalid email or password")
      |> put_flash(:email, String.slice(email, 0, 160))
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
    end
  end

  def update_password(conn, %{"user" => user_params} = params) do
    user = conn.assigns.current_scope.user
    true = Users.sudo_mode?(user)
    {:ok, {_user, expired_tokens}} = Users.update_user_password(user, user_params)

    # disconnect all existing LiveViews with old sessions
    UserAuth.disconnect_sessions(expired_tokens)

    conn
    |> put_session(:user_return_to, ~p"/users/settings")
    |> create(params, "Password updated successfully!")
  end

  def delete(conn, _params) do
    conn
    |> put_flash(:info, "Logged out successfully.")
    |> UserAuth.log_out_user()
  end
end

10	    provider = String.to_existing_atom(provider_str)
11	
12	    case Integrations.authorize_url(provider) do
13	      {:ok, %{url: url, session_params: session_params}} ->
14	        state = Map.get(session_params, "state") || Map.get(session_params, :state)
15	        if state, do: OAuthStateStore.store(state, session_params)
16	
17	        conn

19	        |> redirect(external: url)
20	
21	      {:error, reason} ->
22	        Logger.error("Failed to generate OAuth URL for #{provider}: #{inspect(reason)}")
23	
24	        conn

26	        |> redirect(to: "/")
