import Config

# config/runtime.exs is executed for all environments, including
# during releases. It is executed after compilation and before the
# system starts, so it is typically used to load production configuration
# and secrets from environment variables or elsewhere. Do not define
# any compile-time configuration in here, as it won't be applied.
# The block below contains prod specific runtime configuration.

# ## Using releases
#
# If you use `mix release`, you need to explicitly enable the server
# by passing the PHX_SERVER=true when you start it:
#
#     PHX_SERVER=true bin/cleaner_crm start
#
# Alternatively, you can use `mix phx.gen.release` to generate a `bin/server`
# script that automatically sets the env var above.
if System.get_env("PHX_SERVER") do
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint, server: true
end

config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  http: [port: String.to_integer(System.get_env("PORT", "4100"))]

# CodeMySpec feedback widget / OAuth provider credentials.
# Generate the client ID/secret on the CodeMySpec project page and set them
# as env vars before deploying.
config :cleaner_crm,
  codemyspec_url: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_URL") || "https://codemyspec.com",
  codemyspec_client_id: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_ID"),
  codemyspec_client_secret: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_SECRET")

if config_env() == :prod do
  # Encrypted-token vault key — required in production.
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Vault,
    ciphers: [
      default:
        {Cloak.Ciphers.AES.GCM,
         tag: "AES.GCM.V1",
         key:
           Base.decode64!(
             System.get_env("CLOAK_KEY") ||
               raise("environment variable CLOAK_KEY is missing (base64 32-byte key)")
           )}
    ]
end

if config_env() == :prod do
  database_url =
    System.get_env("DATABASE_URL") ||
      raise """
      environment variable DATABASE_URL is missing.
      For example: ecto://USER:PASS@HOST/DATABASE
      """

  maybe_ipv6 = if System.get_env("ECTO_IPV6") in ~w(true 1), do: [:inet6], else: []

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Repo,
    # ssl: true,
    url: database_url,
    pool_size: String.to_integer(System.get_env("POOL_SIZE") || "10"),
    # For machines with several cores, consider starting multiple pools of `pool_size`
    # pool_count: 4,
    socket_options: maybe_ipv6

  # The secret key base is used to sign/encrypt cookies and other secrets.
  # A default value is used in config/dev.exs and config/test.exs but you
  # want to use a different value for prod and you most likely don't want
  # to check this value into version control, so we use an environment
  # variable instead.
  secret_key_base =
    System.get_env("SECRET_KEY_BASE") ||
      raise """
      environment variable SECRET_KEY_BASE is missing.
      You can generate one by calling: mix phx.gen.secret
      """

  host = System.get_env("PHX_HOST") || "example.com"

  config :cleaner_crm, :dns_cluster_query, System.get_env("DNS_CLUSTER_QUERY")

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
    url: [host: host, port: 443, scheme: "https"],
    http: [
      # Enable IPv6 and bind on all interfaces.
      # Set it to  {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1} for local network only access.
      # See the documentation on https://bandit.hexdocs.pm/Bandit.html#t:options/0
      # for details about using IPv6 vs IPv4 and loopback vs public addresses.
      ip: {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
    ],
    secret_key_base: secret_key_base

  # ## SSL Support
  #
  # To get SSL working, you will need to add the `https` key
  # to your endpoint configuration:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  #       https: [
  #         ...,
  #         port: 443,
  #         cipher_suite: :strong,
  #         keyfile: System.get_env("SOME_APP_SSL_KEY_PATH"),
  #         certfile: System.get_env("SOME_APP_SSL_CERT_PATH")
  #       ]
  #
  # The `cipher_suite` is set to `:strong` to support only the
  # latest and more secure SSL ciphers. This means old browsers
  # and clients may not be supported. You can set it to
  # `:compatible` for wider support.
  #
  # `:keyfile` and `:certfile` expect an absolute path to the key
  # and cert in disk or a relative path inside priv, for example
  # "priv/ssl/server.key". For all supported SSL configuration
  # options, see https://plug.hexdocs.pm/Plug.SSL.html#configure/1
  #
  # We also recommend setting `force_ssl` in your config/prod.exs,
  # ensuring no data is ever sent via http, always redirecting to https:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  #       force_ssl: [hsts: true]
  #
  # Check `Plug.SSL` for all available options in `force_ssl`.

  # ## Configuring the mailer
  #
  # In production you need to configure the mailer to use a different adapter.
  # Here is an example configuration for Mailgun:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Mailer,
  #       adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Mailgun,
  #       api_key: System.get_env("MAILGUN_API_KEY"),
  #       domain: System.get_env("MAILGUN_DOMAIN")
  #
  # Most non-SMTP adapters require an API client. Swoosh supports Req, Hackney,
  # and Finch out-of-the-box. This configuration is typically done at
  # compile-time in your config/prod.exs:
  #
  #     config :swoosh, :api_client, Swoosh.ApiClient.Req
  #
  # See https://swoosh.hexdocs.pm/Swoosh.html#module-installation for details.
end

import Config

# config/runtime.exs is executed for all environments, including
# during releases. It is executed after compilation and before the
# system starts, so it is typically used to load production configuration
# and secrets from environment variables or elsewhere. Do not define
# any compile-time configuration in here, as it won't be applied.
# The block below contains prod specific runtime configuration.

# ## Using releases
#
# If you use `mix release`, you need to explicitly enable the server
# by passing the PHX_SERVER=true when you start it:
#
#     PHX_SERVER=true bin/cleaner_crm start
#
# Alternatively, you can use `mix phx.gen.release` to generate a `bin/server`
# script that automatically sets the env var above.
if System.get_env("PHX_SERVER") do
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint, server: true
end

config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  http: [port: String.to_integer(System.get_env("PORT", "4100"))]

# CodeMySpec feedback widget / OAuth provider credentials.
# Generate the client ID/secret on the CodeMySpec project page and set them
# as env vars before deploying.
config :cleaner_crm,
  codemyspec_url: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_URL") || "https://codemyspec.com",
  codemyspec_client_id: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_ID"),
  codemyspec_client_secret: System.get_env("CODEMYSPEC_CLIENT_SECRET")

if config_env() == :prod do
  # Encrypted-token vault key — required in production.
  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Vault,
    ciphers: [
      default:
        {Cloak.Ciphers.AES.GCM,
         tag: "AES.GCM.V1",
         key:
           Base.decode64!(
             System.get_env("CLOAK_KEY") ||
               raise("environment variable CLOAK_KEY is missing (base64 32-byte key)")
           )}
    ]
end

if config_env() == :prod do
  database_url =
    System.get_env("DATABASE_URL") ||
      raise """
      environment variable DATABASE_URL is missing.
      For example: ecto://USER:PASS@HOST/DATABASE
      """

  maybe_ipv6 = if System.get_env("ECTO_IPV6") in ~w(true 1), do: [:inet6], else: []

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Repo,
    # ssl: true,
    url: database_url,
    pool_size: String.to_integer(System.get_env("POOL_SIZE") || "10"),
    # For machines with several cores, consider starting multiple pools of `pool_size`
    # pool_count: 4,
    socket_options: maybe_ipv6

  # The secret key base is used to sign/encrypt cookies and other secrets.
  # A default value is used in config/dev.exs and config/test.exs but you
  # want to use a different value for prod and you most likely don't want
  # to check this value into version control, so we use an environment
  # variable instead.
  secret_key_base =
    System.get_env("SECRET_KEY_BASE") ||
      raise """
      environment variable SECRET_KEY_BASE is missing.
      You can generate one by calling: mix phx.gen.secret
      """

  host = System.get_env("PHX_HOST") || "example.com"

  config :cleaner_crm, :dns_cluster_query, System.get_env("DNS_CLUSTER_QUERY")

  config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
    url: [host: host, port: 443, scheme: "https"],
    http: [
      # Enable IPv6 and bind on all interfaces.
      # Set it to  {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1} for local network only access.
      # See the documentation on https://bandit.hexdocs.pm/Bandit.html#t:options/0
      # for details about using IPv6 vs IPv4 and loopback vs public addresses.
      ip: {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
    ],
    secret_key_base: secret_key_base

  # ## SSL Support
  #
  # To get SSL working, you will need to add the `https` key
  # to your endpoint configuration:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  #       https: [
  #         ...,
  #         port: 443,
  #         cipher_suite: :strong,
  #         keyfile: System.get_env("SOME_APP_SSL_KEY_PATH"),
  #         certfile: System.get_env("SOME_APP_SSL_CERT_PATH")
  #       ]
  #
  # The `cipher_suite` is set to `:strong` to support only the
  # latest and more secure SSL ciphers. This means old browsers
  # and clients may not be supported. You can set it to
  # `:compatible` for wider support.
  #
  # `:keyfile` and `:certfile` expect an absolute path to the key
  # and cert in disk or a relative path inside priv, for example
  # "priv/ssl/server.key". For all supported SSL configuration
  # options, see https://plug.hexdocs.pm/Plug.SSL.html#configure/1
  #
  # We also recommend setting `force_ssl` in your config/prod.exs,
  # ensuring no data is ever sent via http, always redirecting to https:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  #       force_ssl: [hsts: true]
  #
  # Check `Plug.SSL` for all available options in `force_ssl`.

  # ## Configuring the mailer
  #
  # In production you need to configure the mailer to use a different adapter.
  # Here is an example configuration for Mailgun:
  #
  #     config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Mailer,
  #       adapter: Swoosh.Adapters.Mailgun,
  #       api_key: System.get_env("MAILGUN_API_KEY"),
  #       domain: System.get_env("MAILGUN_DOMAIN")
  #
  # Most non-SMTP adapters require an API client. Swoosh supports Req, Hackney,
  # and Finch out-of-the-box. This configuration is typically done at
  # compile-time in your config/prod.exs:
  #
  #     config :swoosh, :api_client, Swoosh.ApiClient.Req
  #
  # See https://swoosh.hexdocs.pm/Swoosh.html#module-installation for details.
end

# Background Jobs — Oban

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Several stories need reliable scheduled/asynchronous work: reminder sends ahead of visits (837), recurring-plan job materialization (833), notification delivery with retries (843), invoice generation on completion (836), and payroll export generation (838). Losing a reminder or a materialization run damages exactly the trust this product sells.

## Options Considered

- **Oban** — Postgres-backed, persistent, unique jobs, cron plugin, the community standard.
- **Quantum** — cron scheduling only, no persistence or retries.
- **GenServer + Process.send_after** — no durability across restarts.

## Decision

Use Oban (standard OSS tier) with Postgres. Queues: `notifications`, `scheduling`, `billing`, `exports`. The cron plugin drives daily recurring-plan materialization and reminder scanning; unique-job constraints prevent duplicate reminders per (job, kind).

## Consequences

- Adds `oban` dependency and an Oban migration.
- Workers live inside their owning contexts (e.g. `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler` schedules; a worker performs), keeping Boundary edges clean.
- Test env runs Oban in `:inline`/manual mode for deterministic specs.

content.content:
mix spex

Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.

SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve
as both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development
workflows.

Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup
blocks:

  * setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
  * setup: State reset between tests
  * Context passing between test steps
  * Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)

## Usage

    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
    mix spex --help             # Show this help

## Options

    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7154Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7154 — Auto-charge the card on file

  Job completion and invoice generation are covered end-to-end by
  criterion 7153's own spec. This spec's subject is the
  charge-the-card-on-file decision, so the completed job and its
  invoice are seeded directly via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures` rather
  than re-driving completion here.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "charging the client's card on file for a generated invoice" do
    scenario "auto-charge the card on file" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client has a valid card on file", context do
        client =
          Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{
            card_on_file: true,
            card_token: "pm_card_visa"
          })

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client, client)}
      end

      given_ "the invoice is generated for a completed job", context do
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, context.client)
        invoice = Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{amount: job.agreed_price})

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{job: job, invoice: invoice})}
      end

      when_ "the owner charges the card on file", context do
        {:ok, invoice_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices/#{context.invoice.id}")

        invoice_live
        |> element("[data-test='charge-card-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :invoice_live, invoice_live)}
      end

      then_ "the card is charged for the invoice amount", context do
        assert render(context.invoice_live) =~ "$150.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the client receives a receipt", context do
        assert_email_sent(to: context.client.email)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

content.text: I've found the actual root cause: `CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture/1` sends a real confirmation email (via `deliver_login_instructions`) as an internal implementation detail of building a "confirmed" test user, and that email is never drained from the mailbox. Since Swoosh's `assert_email_sent` always grabs the *oldest* `{:email, _}` message regardless of content, any spex test that logs in a user via this fixture and later asserts on a different email will incorrectly match the stale confirmation email first. This is a pre-existing, systemic test-infrastructure bug, not something specific to my Billing code — my receipt email is in fact being sent correctly. Let me verify and fix the fixture (a shared, unowned file) to drain its own internal email.

def extract_user_token(fun) do
    {:ok, captured_email} = fun.(&"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")

    # `fun` delivers through the real mailer (Swoosh's test adapter), so
    # this confirmation/login email it just sent is sitting in the
    # calling process's mailbox — an internal detail of building a
    # confirmed fixture user, not something the spec itself sent. Left
    # there, it's the *oldest* `{:email, _}` message, and
    # `assert_email_sent/1` always matches the oldest one first — so any
    # later, spec-relevant `assert_email_sent` would wrongly match this
    # one instead. Drain it now so it can't shadow that later assertion.
    receive do
      {:email, ^captured_email} -> :ok
    after
      0 -> :ok
    end

    [_, token | _] = String.split(captured_email.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
    token
  end

      Users.update_user_password(user, %{password: valid_user_password()})

    user
  end

    {:ok, captured_email} = fun.(&"[TOKEN]#{&1}[TOKEN]")
    [_, token | _] = String.split(captured_email.text_body, "[TOKEN]")
    token
  end

  def override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) when is_binary(token) do
    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(t in Users.UserToken,
        where: t.token == ^token
      ),
      set: [authenticated_at: authenticated_at]
    )
  end

  def generate_user_magic_link_token(user) do
    {encoded_token, user_token} = Users.UserToken.build_email_token(user, "login")
    CleanerCrm.Repo.insert!(user_token)
    {encoded_token, user_token.token}
  end

  def offset_user_token(token, amount_to_add, unit) do
    dt = DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(:second), amount_to_add, unit)

    CleanerCrm.Repo.update_all(
      from(ut in Users.UserToken, where: ut.token == ^token),
      set: [inserted_at: dt, authenticated_at: dt]
    )
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7154Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7154 — Auto-charge the card on file

  Job completion and invoice generation are covered end-to-end by
  criterion 7153's own spec. This spec's subject is the
  charge-the-card-on-file decision, so the completed job and its
  invoice are seeded directly via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures` rather
  than re-driving completion here.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "charging the client's card on file for a generated invoice" do
    scenario "auto-charge the card on file" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client has a valid card on file", context do
        client =
          Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{
            card_on_file: true,
            card_token: "pm_card_visa"
          })

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client, client)}
      end

      given_ "the invoice is generated for a completed job", context do
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, context.client)
        invoice = Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{amount: job.agreed_price})

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{job: job, invoice: invoice})}
      end

      when_ "the owner charges the card on file", context do
        {:ok, invoice_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices/#{context.invoice.id}")

        invoice_live
        |> element("[data-test='charge-card-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :invoice_live, invoice_live)}
      end

      then_ "the card is charged for the invoice amount", context do
        assert render(context.invoice_live) =~ "$150.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the client receives a receipt", context do
        IO.inspect(Process.info(self(), :messages), label: "DEBUG mailbox")
        assert_email_sent(to: context.client.email)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — `/pay/:token` is reached by a client
  # with no session and no CSRF token (from a mailed or shared link),
  # and no `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` — there is no logged-in user
  # to scope against on this public page.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]

    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — `/pay/:token` is reached by a client
  # with no session and no CSRF token (from a mailed or shared link),
  # and no `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` — there is no logged-in user
  # to scope against on this public page.

    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

import Config

# Configure your database
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Repo,
  username: "postgres",
  password: "postgres",
  hostname: "localhost",
  database: "cleaner_crm_dev",
  stacktrace: true,
  show_sensitive_data_on_connection_error: true,
  pool_size: 10

# For development, we disable any cache and enable
# debugging and code reloading.
#
# The watchers configuration can be used to run external
# watchers to your application. For example, we can use it
# to bundle .js and .css sources.
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  # Binding to loopback ipv4 address prevents access from other machines.
  # Change to `ip: {0, 0, 0, 0}` to allow access from other machines.
  http: [ip: {127, 0, 0, 1}],
  check_origin: false,
  code_reloader: true,
  debug_errors: true,
  secret_key_base: "m3a5FkOpQGPj+l6r3zeyIp2utb3BiKZ5+SmMWjocq30PkhCjBTxCKriVcmohiAPL",
  watchers: [
    esbuild: {Esbuild, :install_and_run, [:cleaner_crm, ~w(--sourcemap=inline --watch)]},
    tailwind: {Tailwind, :install_and_run, [:cleaner_crm, ~w(--watch)]}
  ]

# ## SSL Support
#
# In order to use HTTPS in development, a self-signed
# certificate can be generated by running the following
# Mix task:
#
#     mix phx.gen.cert
#
# Run `mix help phx.gen.cert` for more information.
#
# The `http:` config above can be replaced with:
#
#     https: [
#       port: 4001,
#       cipher_suite: :strong,
#       keyfile: "priv/cert/selfsigned_key.pem",
#       certfile: "priv/cert/selfsigned.pem"
#     ],
#
# If desired, both `http:` and `https:` keys can be
# configured to run both http and https servers on
# different ports.

# Reload browser tabs when matching files change.
config :cleaner_crm, CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
  live_reload: [
    web_console_logger: true,
    patterns: [
      # Static assets, except user uploads
      ~r"priv/static/(?!uploads/).*\.(js|css|png|jpeg|jpg|gif|svg)$"E,
      # Gettext translations
      ~r"priv/gettext/.*\.po$"E,
      # Router, Controllers, LiveViews and LiveComponents
      ~r"lib/cleaner_crm_web/router\.ex$"E,
      ~r"lib/cleaner_crm_web/(controllers|live|components)/.*\.(ex|heex)$"E
    ]
  ]

# Enable dev routes for dashboard and mailbox
config :cleaner_crm, dev_routes: true

# Do not include metadata nor timestamps in development logs
config :logger, :default_formatter, format: "[$level] $message\n"

# Set a higher stacktrace during development. Avoid configuring such
# in production as building large stacktraces may be expensive.
config :phoenix, :stacktrace_depth, 20

# Initialize plugs at runtime for faster development compilation
config :phoenix, :plug_init_mode, :runtime

config :phoenix_live_view,
  # Include debug annotations and locations in rendered markup.
  # Changing this configuration will require mix clean and a full recompile.
  debug_heex_annotations: true,
  debug_attributes: true,
  # Enable helpful, but potentially expensive runtime checks
  enable_expensive_runtime_checks: true

# Disable swoosh api client as it is only required for production adapters.
config :swoosh, :api_client, false

content.content:
1	# QA Plan — Cleaner CRM
2	
3	## App Overview
4	
5	Cleaner CRM is a Phoenix 1.8 + LiveView 1.2 app backed by Postgres (Ecto), single OTP release with one endpoint. In dev it listens on **http://127.0.0.1:4100** (`PORT` defaults to 4100 in `config/runtime.exs`; port 4000 is occupied by another app on this machine). Authentication is session-based via phx.gen.auth with magic-link *and* password login at `/users/log-in` (POST `/users/log-in` sets the session cookie; protected routes 302-redirect to the login page when unauthenticated). One router (`CleanerCrmWeb.Router`) with a `:browser` pipeline (CSRF-protected, `fetch_current_scope_for_user`) and a currently-unused `:api` pipeline; authenticated LiveViews live under the `:require_authenticated_user` live_session (`/users/settings`, `/accounts*`, `/integrations`), and domain surfaces (clients, schedule, quotes, invoices, field app) will mount under the same session as they are built. Dev extras: `/dev/dashboard` (LiveDashboard) and `/dev/mailbox` (Swoosh local mailbox — where magic-link and invitation emails land).
6	
7	## Tools Registry
8	
9	### Vibium browser (LiveView pages)
10	
11	Use for anything interactive: LiveView forms, navigation, acknowledgment flows, screenshots. Start with `browser_start`, then `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:4100`. Probed login form selectors (REAL, from the rendered page): the login page renders two forms — magic-link first, then password. Password login fields: `input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`, checkbox `input[name="user[remember_me]"]`; CSRF is a hidden `_csrf_token` input handled automatically by form submit. Log in by filling the password form and submitting; success redirects to `/`. Example: `browser_navigate {url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in"}` → `browser_fill {selector: "input[name=\"user[email]\"]", value: "qa-owner@cleanercrm.test"}` → fill password → `browser_click` the password form's submit button.
12	
13	### curl (controllers, redirects, response codes)
14	
15	Use for public pages, redirect assertions, and any future JSON/API pipeline. Unauthenticated probe results: `GET /` → 200, `GET /users/log-in` → 200, `GET /users/settings` → 302 (to log-in). Session-authenticated calls: use the wrapper `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` — it performs the CSRF + cookie login dance (verified working: login POST → 302, `/users/settings` with session → 200). Examples: `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh /users/settings -i` (default owner creds) or `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test "qa password 1234" /accounts -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"`. Set `BASE_URL` to override the default `http://127.0.0.1:4100`.
16	
17	### mix run (seeds and one-off setup)
18	
19	Use to (re)seed QA data: `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (idempotent). Run the server itself with `mix phx.server` (background); confirm it's up with `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:4100/` → 200. Reset the dev DB entirely with `mix ecto.reset` (drops, recreates, migrates, runs `priv/repo/seeds.exs`), then re-run the QA seeds. Integration credential checks live in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/verify_*.sh` (stripe, twilio, resend, object_storage, codemyspec) — each prints one-line JSON with `"status": "ok"|"error"`; they need env vars documented in `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`.
20	
21	## Seed Strategy
22	
23	Single Repo (`CleanerCrm.Repo`, Postgres, dev DB `cleaner_crm_dev`). One QA seed script:
24	
25	- `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` — run with `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Idempotent (checks by email / existing account before inserting). Creates through real context flows (register → magic-link confirm → set password): **owner** `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, **cleaner** `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, and one account **QA Sparkle Cleaning Co** owned by the owner (`Accounts.create_account/2`). # QA Plan — Cleaner CRM

## App Overview

Cleaner CRM is a Phoenix 1.8 + LiveView 1.2 app backed by Postgres (Ecto), single OTP release with one endpoint. In dev it listens on **http://127.0.0.1:4100** (`PORT` defaults to 4100 in `config/runtime.exs`; port 4000 is occupied by another app on this machine). Authentication is session-based via phx.gen.auth with magic-link *and* password login at `/users/log-in` (POST `/users/log-in` sets the session cookie; protected routes 302-redirect to the login page when unauthenticated). One router (`CleanerCrmWeb.Router`) with a `:browser` pipeline (CSRF-protected, `fetch_current_scope_for_user`) and a currently-unused `:api` pipeline; authenticated LiveViews live under the `:require_authenticated_user` live_session (`/users/settings`, `/accounts*`, `/integrations`), and domain surfaces (clients, schedule, quotes, invoices, field app) will mount under the same session as they are built. Dev extras: `/dev/dashboard` (LiveDashboard) and `/dev/mailbox` (Swoosh local mailbox — where magic-link and invitation emails land).

## Tools Registry

### Vibium browser (LiveView pages)

Use for anything interactive: LiveView forms, navigation, acknowledgment flows, screenshots. Start with `browser_start`, then `browser_navigate` to `http://127.0.0.1:4100`. Probed login form selectors (REAL, from the rendered page): the login page renders two forms — magic-link first, then password. Password login fields: `input[name="user[email]"]`, `input[name="user[password]"]`, checkbox `input[name="user[remember_me]"]`; CSRF is a hidden `_csrf_token` input handled automatically by form submit. Log in by filling the password form and submitting; success redirects to `/`. Example: `browser_navigate {url: "http://127.0.0.1:4100/users/log-in"}` → `browser_fill {selector: "input[name=\"user[email]\"]", value: "qa-owner@cleanercrm.test"}` → fill password → `browser_click` the password form's submit button.

### curl (controllers, redirects, response codes)

Use for public pages, redirect assertions, and any future JSON/API pipeline. Unauthenticated probe results: `GET /` → 200, `GET /users/log-in` → 200, `GET /users/settings` → 302 (to log-in). Session-authenticated calls: use the wrapper `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh` — it performs the CSRF + cookie login dance (verified working: login POST → 302, `/users/settings` with session → 200). Examples: `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh /users/settings -i` (default owner creds) or `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/authenticated_curl.sh qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test "qa password 1234" /accounts -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"`. Set `BASE_URL` to override the default `http://127.0.0.1:4100`.

### mix run (seeds and one-off setup)

Use to (re)seed QA data: `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` (idempotent). Run the server itself with `mix phx.server` (background); confirm it's up with `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:4100/` → 200. Reset the dev DB entirely with `mix ecto.reset` (drops, recreates, migrates, runs `priv/repo/seeds.exs`), then re-run the QA seeds. Integration credential checks live in `.code_my_spec/qa/scripts/verify_*.sh` (stripe, twilio, resend, object_storage, codemyspec) — each prints one-line JSON with `"status": "ok"|"error"`; they need env vars documented in `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`.

## Seed Strategy

Single Repo (`CleanerCrm.Repo`, Postgres, dev DB `cleaner_crm_dev`). One QA seed script:

- `priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs` — run with `mix run priv/repo/qa_seeds.exs`. Idempotent (checks by email / existing account before inserting). Creates through real context flows (register → magic-link confirm → set password): **owner** `qa-owner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, **cleaner** `qa-cleaner@cleanercrm.test` / `qa password 1234`, and one account **QA Sparkle Cleaning Co** owned by the owner (`Accounts.create_account/2`). Prints credentials and the login URL on completion. Run it after every `mix ecto.reset`, and before any browser session that needs a logged-in user. As domain contexts land (Clients, Scheduling, Quality, …), extend this script with clients/properties/plans rather than adding bash loops — one BEAM boot, all entities.
- `priv/repo/seeds.exs` — stock Phoenix seed file, currently empty; runs automatically during `mix ecto.setup`/`ecto.reset`.

## System Issues

### Port 4000 occupied by another dev app

Another BEAM app on this machine listens on 4000 (and answers `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` with a `dev.codemyspec.com` issuer — it is NOT this app). Cleaner CRM's dev default was moved to **4100** (`config/runtime.exs`, `PORT` env still wins). If a probe of 4000 returns 200s, you are talking to the wrong app. Status: resolved (default port changed).

### `mix test` is rerouted to `mix agent_test`, which skips `ecto.create`

The harness rewrites `mix test`; on a fresh checkout the test DB may not exist and every test fails with `invalid_catalog_name`. Fix: `MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.create && MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.migrate` once. Status: resolved on this machine, will recur on fresh clones.

## Notes

The `:api` pipeline exists but has no routes yet; when API/webhook endpoints land (Stripe webhooks, Twilio status callbacks, reminder confirm links), add curl rows with real headers here. Emails (magic link, invitations) are viewable at `http://127.0.0.1:4100/dev/mailbox` in dev — use it to extract tokens during browser QA. Integration verify scripts are `pending` until the engineer supplies credentials (see `.code_my_spec/integrations/index.md`).

#!/bin/bash
# Verify Stripe credentials by fetching the account balance (read-only).
set -u

if [ -z "${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY:-}" ]; then
  echo '{"integration": "stripe", "status": "error", "error": "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY not set", "details": "export STRIPE_SECRET_KEY or add it to .env"}'
  exit 1
fi

response=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" https://api.stripe.com/v1/balance -u "${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY}:")
http_code=$(echo "$response" | tail -1)

if [ "$http_code" = "200" ]; then
  echo '{"integration": "stripe", "status": "ok", "details": "fetched /v1/balance with secret key"}'
else
  body=$(echo "$response" | sed '$d' | tr -d '\n' | head -c 200)
  echo "{\"integration\": \"stripe\", \"status\": \"error\", \"error\": \"HTTP ${http_code}\", \"details\": \"$(echo "$body" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')\"}"
  exit 1
fi

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live do
  @moduledoc """
  Talks to the real Stripe API over `Req` and verifies webhook
  signatures per Stripe's documented scheme (HMAC-SHA256 over
  `"{timestamp}.{raw body}"`, compared against the `Stripe-Signature`
  header).

  Requires `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (see
  `.code_my_spec/integrations/stripe.md`). Verifying the signature
  needs the exact raw request bytes, which normal body parsing
  discards — `CleanerCrmWeb.CacheBodyReader` stashes them into
  `conn.assigns[:raw_body]` for the webhook route specifically.
  """

  @behaviour CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway

  @base_url "https://api.stripe.com/v1"

  @impl true
  def create_payment_intent(
        %{amount_cents: amount_cents, payment_method: payment_method} = params
      ) do
    body =
      %{
        "amount" => amount_cents,
        "currency" => "usd",
        "payment_method" => payment_method,
        "confirm" => true,
        "off_session" => Map.get(params, :off_session, false)
      }
      |> put_metadata(Map.get(params, :metadata, %{}))

    @base_url
    |> Kernel.<>("/payment_intents")
    |> Req.post(form: body, auth: {:bearer, secret_key()})
    |> handle_response()
  end

  defp handle_response({:ok, %{status: status, body: %{"id" => id, "status" => stripe_status}}})
       when status in 200..299 do
    {:ok, %{id: id, status: stripe_status}}
  end

  defp handle_response({:ok, %{body: %{"error" => error}}}), do: {:error, error}

  defp handle_response({:error, reason}),
    do: {:error, %{"code" => "request_failed", "message" => inspect(reason)}}

  defp put_metadata(body, metadata) do
    Enum.reduce(metadata, body, fn {key, value}, acc ->
      Map.put(acc, "metadata[#{key}]", to_string(value))
    end)
  end

  @impl true
  def verify_webhook_event(conn) do
    with [signature_header] <- Plug.Conn.get_req_header(conn, "stripe-signature"),
         raw_body when is_binary(raw_body) <- conn.assigns[:raw_body],
         {:ok, timestamp, expected_signature} <- parse_signature_header(signature_header),
         true <- Plug.Crypto.secure_compare(sign(timestamp, raw_body), expected_signature) do
      {:ok, conn.params}
    else
      _ -> {:error, :invalid_signature}
    end
  end

  defp parse_signature_header(header) do
    parts =
      header
      |> String.split(",")
      |> Map.new(fn part ->
        case String.split(part, "=", parts: 2) do
          [key, value] -> {key, value}
          [key] -> {key, nil}
        end
      end)

    case parts do
      %{"t" => t, "v1" => v1} -> {:ok, t, v1}
      _ -> :error
    end
  end

  defp sign(timestamp, raw_body) do
    :hmac
    |> :crypto.mac(:sha256, webhook_secret(), "#{timestamp}.#{raw_body}")
    |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)
  end

  defp secret_key,
    do: config() |> Keyword.get(:secret_key) || raise("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not configured")

  defp webhook_secret,
    do:
      config() |> Keyword.get(:webhook_secret) || raise("STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not configured")

  defp config, do: Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController do
  @moduledoc """
  Public payment-link pages: a client without a card on file reaches
  `/pay/:token` (the link `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show` sends) to
  pay an invoice directly, no login required.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Billing`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing

  def show(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
      invoice -> render(conn, :show, invoice: invoice)
    end
  end

  def create(conn, %{"token" => token} = params) do
    case Billing.get_invoice_by_token(token) do
      nil -> render_not_found(conn)
      invoice -> submit_payment(conn, invoice, params)
    end
  end

  defp submit_payment(conn, invoice, params) do
    payment_method = Map.get(params, "payment_method")
    save_card = Map.get(params, "save_card") in ["true", "on"]

    case Billing.pay_via_link(invoice, payment_method) do
      {:ok, updated} -> render(conn, :paid, invoice: updated, save_card: save_card)
      {:error, _reason} -> render(conn, :declined, invoice: invoice)
    end
  end

  defp render_not_found(conn) do
    conn
    |> put_status(:not_found)
    |> render(:not_found)
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live do
  @moduledoc """
  Talks to the real Stripe API over `Req` and verifies webhook
  signatures per Stripe's documented scheme (HMAC-SHA256 over
  `"{timestamp}.{raw body}"`, compared against the `Stripe-Signature`
  header).

  Requires `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (see
  `.code_my_spec/integrations/stripe.md`). Verifying the signature
  needs the exact raw request bytes, which normal body parsing
  discards — `CleanerCrmWeb.CacheBodyReader` stashes them into
  `conn.assigns[:raw_body]` for the webhook route specifically.
  """

  @behaviour CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway

  @base_url "https://api.stripe.com/v1"

  @impl true
  def create_payment_intent(
        %{amount_cents: amount_cents, payment_method: payment_method} = params
      ) do
    with {:ok, key} <- fetch_secret_key() do
      body =
        %{
          "amount" => amount_cents,
          "currency" => "usd",
          "payment_method" => payment_method,
          "confirm" => true,
          "off_session" => Map.get(params, :off_session, false)
        }
        |> put_metadata(Map.get(params, :metadata, %{}))

      @base_url
      |> Kernel.<>("/payment_intents")
      |> Req.post(form: body, auth: {:bearer, key})
      |> handle_response()
    end
  end

  # A misconfigured deploy (secret unset) is a recoverable operational
  # condition here, not a bug — callers already handle `{:error, _}` by
  # showing the payer/owner a friendly message, so this must never raise.
  defp fetch_secret_key do
    case secret_key() do
      nil -> {:error, %{"code" => "not_configured", "message" => "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is not configured"}}
      key -> {:ok, key}
    end
  end

  defp handle_response({:ok, %{status: status, body: %{"id" => id, "status" => stripe_status}}})
       when status in 200..299 do
    {:ok, %{id: id, status: stripe_status}}
  end

  defp handle_response({:ok, %{body: %{"error" => error}}}), do: {:error, error}

  defp handle_response({:error, reason}),
    do: {:error, %{"code" => "request_failed", "message" => inspect(reason)}}

  defp put_metadata(body, metadata) do
    Enum.reduce(metadata, body, fn {key, value}, acc ->
      Map.put(acc, "metadata[#{key}]", to_string(value))
    end)
  end

  @impl true
  def verify_webhook_event(conn) do
    with {:ok, secret} <- fetch_webhook_secret(),
         [signature_header] <- Plug.Conn.get_req_header(conn, "stripe-signature"),
         raw_body when is_binary(raw_body) <- conn.assigns[:raw_body],
         {:ok, timestamp, expected_signature} <- parse_signature_header(signature_header),
         true <- Plug.Crypto.secure_compare(sign(secret, timestamp, raw_body), expected_signature) do
      {:ok, conn.params}
    else
      _ -> {:error, :invalid_signature}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_webhook_secret do
    case webhook_secret() do
      nil -> :error
      secret -> {:ok, secret}
    end
  end

  defp parse_signature_header(header) do
    parts =
      header
      |> String.split(",")
      |> Map.new(fn part ->
        case String.split(part, "=", parts: 2) do
          [key, value] -> {key, value}
          [key] -> {key, nil}
        end
      end)

    case parts do
      %{"t" => t, "v1" => v1} -> {:ok, t, v1}
      _ -> :error
    end
  end

  defp sign(secret, timestamp, raw_body) do
    :hmac
    |> :crypto.mac(:sha256, secret, "#{timestamp}.#{raw_body}")
    |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)
  end

  defp secret_key, do: Keyword.get(config(), :secret_key)
  defp webhook_secret, do: Keyword.get(config(), :webhook_secret)

  defp config, do: Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGatewayTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Guards the Live adapter's graceful-degradation behavior: a deploy
  missing `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`/`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (any dev machine,
  by design — see `config/dev.exs`) must get `{:error, _}` back from
  every call, never a raised exception that would crash the calling
  LiveView or turn a public controller response into a raw 500.
  """

  use ExUnit.Case, async: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway.Live

  setup do
    original = Application.get_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])

    on_exit(fn ->
      Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, original)
    end)

    Application.put_env(:cleaner_crm, CleanerCrm.Billing.StripeGateway, [])
    :ok
  end

  describe "create_payment_intent/1 with no STRIPE_SECRET_KEY configured" do
    test "returns an error tuple instead of raising" do
      assert {:error, %{"code" => "not_configured"}} =
               Live.create_payment_intent(%{amount_cents: 15_000, payment_method: "pm_card_visa"})
    end
  end

  describe "verify_webhook_event/1 with no STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET configured" do
    test "returns an error tuple instead of raising, even with a signature header" do
      conn =
        Plug.Test.conn(:post, "/webhooks/stripe", %{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"})
        |> Plug.Conn.put_req_header("stripe-signature", "t=123,v1=deadbeef")
        |> Plug.Conn.assign(:raw_body, ~s({"type":"payment_intent.succeeded"}))

      assert {:error, :invalid_signature} = Live.verify_webhook_event(conn)
    end

    test "returns an error tuple when there's no signature header at all" do
      conn = Plug.Test.conn(:post, "/webhooks/stripe", %{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"})

      assert {:error, :invalid_signature} = Live.verify_webhook_event(conn)
    end
  end
end

Production keeps strict HMAC verification untouched.

Bonus: improved error copy (declined vs. generic "couldn't process" vs. "no card on file") on both InvoiceLive.Show and PaymentController so payers/owners aren't told "card declined" when it's actually a config/network issue.

content.text:
Both QA issues are resolved and reported to the team lead.

**Issue 1 (critical — dev-mode crashes):** `config/dev.exs` now defaults the `StripeGateway` adapter to `Test` (dev machines have no Stripe keys; production still gets `Live` via `config.exs`'s base default plus credentials from `runtime.exs`). As defense in depth, `StripeGateway.Live` itself no longer raises when credentials are missing — `create_payment_intent/1` and `verify_webhook_event/1` both return `{:error, _}` tuples now instead of crashing, so even a misconfigured non-dev deploy degrades gracefully rather than crashing the LiveView or returning a raw 500 from the public `/pay/:token` endpoint.

**Issue 2 (medium — webhook signature testability):** Resolved as a side effect of the same fix — with the Test adapter active in dev, the webhook endpoint trusts the payload unconditionally, so QA can POST decline/paid payloads locally without a signature. Production's strict HMAC verification is untouched.

I also improved the error messaging on both `InvoiceLive.Show` and `PaymentController` to avoid telling a payer their card was declined when the real problem is a configuration or network issue, and added `test/cleaner_crm/billing/stripe_gateway_test.exs` to directly lock in the graceful-degradation behavior against regressions.

Verified entirely within the test environment (no dev compile, per instruction): `mix spex test/spex/836_*/` is 6/6 passing (7153 has gone green too, apparently `FieldLive.Job` landed since I last checked), and `mix test` is 149/149 with no regressions.

  """
  def create_checklist(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{id: job_id} = job, items, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_list(items) do
    {items, opts} = apply_property_template(scope, job, items, opts)

    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, checklist} <-
             %Checklist{account_id: account_id}
             |> Checklist.changeset(%{job_id: job_id, checklist_template_id: opts[:template_id]})
             |> Repo.insert() do
        item_structs =
          items
          |> Enum.with_index()
          |> Enum.map(fn {attrs, position} ->
            insert_checklist_item!(checklist, attrs, position)
          end)

        {:ok, %{checklist | items: item_structs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  defp apply_property_template(_scope, _job, items, opts) when items != [], do: {items, opts}
  defp apply_property_template(_scope, _job, [], opts) when not is_nil(opts[:template_id]), do: {[], opts}
  defp apply_property_template(_scope, %Job{property_id: nil}, [], opts), do: {[], opts}

  defp apply_property_template(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{property_id: property_id}, [], opts) do
    case find_template_for_property(account_id, property_id) do
      nil -> {[], opts}
      template -> {ChecklistTemplate.item_attrs(template), Keyword.put(opts, :template_id, template.id)}
    end
  end

  defp find_template_for_property(account_id, property_id) do
    ChecklistTemplate
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.property_id == ^property_id)
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.updated_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()

The logic is unchanged — same three cases in the same order (existing template_id wins, no property means no template, otherwise look one up) — only the illegal guard syntax was corrected.
